prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick), Main Transformer, export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; operational/dispatch boundary; local systems run turbines; authorized signals with transmission system). Public grid, non-farm port ops out of scope. Personnel keep safety authority. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; within limits; blocks protection-conflicting commands; produces Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode if aux lost), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; blade imagery). Substation: Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; emergency bus). Aux power: auto start on loss; transfer within V/f limits; no unapproved paralleling; not exported; nonessential shed; start-failure alarm; UPS control power; transfer back when stable. Grid: Grid Dispatcher sets dispatch per agreement; Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard) allocates output, uses Position Quality Flag for movement planning; Control Engineer verifies settings; frequency response only in authorized mode; comms loss keeps local protection; Grid Constraint may reduce/disconnect; normal export resumes only when interface stable and protections available; Substation Operator confirms switching; alarms safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; work packages from Pitch Deviation Notice; produces Session Revocation Receipt), Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; marine ops/restrictions overview), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; ranks work by condition, safety, production, access, resources; uses Squall Window Bulletin), Operations Radio Console, Work Permit Portal (checked before controlled-work release). Marine: Marine Coordinator (daily plan, conflicts, distributes changes), Duty Planner, Vessel Master (departure readiness), Weather Service (forecasts), Weather Analyst advises Marine Coordinator; Weather Hold mode when limits unsafe; Port Agent; Rescue Coordinator; HSE Officer produces Harness Audit Card before transfer; Storekeeper. Vessels: Crew Transfer Vessel (Kestrel Bay; within limits), Daughter Craft (reviewed use only), Service Operations Vessel; Helideck; Vessel AIS Receiver (Blue Granite; produces Position Quality Flag). Personnel Tracking Console (roster); North/South Access Scanners; Warehouse System (Mosslight; inventory; Backorder Exception Slip); Spares Hub; Metocean Buoy (Copper Finch; sea conditions; Wave Burst Record). Cybersecurity Gateway (Quiet Harbor):

Document units:
S247: The Duty Planner reviews the ranked queue and confirms that urgent work has a clear technical basis and a feasible execution path.
S248: Confirmed faults that threaten personnel safety or cause substantial generation loss receive priority over routine inspections.
S249: Planned work is advanced when its due date, condition evidence, and operational value justify the required outage or vessel time.
S250: The Nacelle Condition Monitor provides condition data that helps distinguish developing degradation from transient alarms.
S251: The Turbine Sensor Bus provides operating measurements for work that depends on recent machine behavior.
S252: The Export Cable Monitor helps planners assess whether cable condition warrants inspection or corrective intervention.
S253: The Field Supervisor checks reported faults against available evidence and identifies work that requires an offshore visit.
S254: The Blade Inspection Drone can support inspection planning when blade access from a vessel or by rope team is not justified.
S255: The Weather Service supplies forecast information for evaluating marine and aviation access options.
S256: The Weather Analyst reviews forecast confidence and highlights conditions that could invalidate a planned access period.
S257: The Marine Coordinator compares expected access conditions with vessel capability, transit time, and worksite limits.
S258: The Duty Planner considers Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel, and Helideck access when selecting a mobilization method.
S259: A Weather Hold prevents mobilization when forecast or observed conditions exceed the approved operating limits.
S260: Sable Orchard assigns vessel and crew resources to approved work packages after the Duty Planner confirms the operating priority.
S261: The Marine Coordinator coordinates resource changes with the Vessel Master and affected work teams.
S262: The Storekeeper uses the exception slip to validate an unavailable part before the work package is rescheduled.
S263: The Duty Planner accounts for part availability, technician competence, and estimated task duration before committing a work window.
S264: Work packages with long lead requirements are scheduled early enough to avoid avoidable vessel standby and repeat mobilization.
S265: The Work Permit Portal supports readiness checks for work requiring controlled access or electrical isolation.
S266: The HSE Officer reviews hazards and confirms that proposed controls match the task scope and site conditions.
S267: The Offshore Substation sends a Transformer Tap Snapshot when a transformer condition review is requested.
S268: The Substation Operator confirms local operating constraints before substation work is placed in the executable plan.
